Reviewing (mostly) every game (or DLC) in my library, part 637:

⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️☆☆ (8/10)

[i]Marvel’s Spider-Man Remastered[/i] is just ... it's just pure fun. Like, the game is eager and upfront about wanting the player to [i]feel[/i] like a superhero and be [i]cool[/i] and [i]have fun[/i]. Oh, to be young again. 

I mean, I could honestly leave the review at that. But seriously, I never saw the appeal of Spider-Man (also, I thought it was "Spiderman?"). Peter Parker seemed like a nice kid, but he doesn't have the aura of Batman or Superman. His powers also seemed weak—shooting webs and gymnastics can't hold a candle to Batman's fancy technology or Superman's literal superpowers. But I get it, now! I do! There's a sense of limitless joy when playing the game. The gameplay is addictive and reminiscent of the [i]Arkham[/i] series; the story and cast are surprisingly likeable; and the game is great on Deck. I do have to point out, however, the repetitive nature of the game. The map is filled with Ubisoft-style challenges that require multiple stages of completion. The side content is also noticeably weak, and though I had a blast, I'm going to deem [i]Spider-Man[/i] completed at around the 70% mark.

[b][h2]Pros:[/h2][/b]
✅ [b]Action.[/b] The combat is clearly inspired by the Batman games, but it carves out its own identity through Spider-Man's gadgets, web abilities, and incredible mobility. It's a pretty familiar formula: fast, fluid fights that reward combos. Yet, you're encouraged to mix attacks, gadgets, air combos, and environmental takedowns instead of relying on a single strategy. Usually, the physical portion in games has the most love devoted to it, but I honestly relied on Spidey's gadgets half the time—they're STRONG. 

✅ [b]Traversal.[/b] I usually hate the "empty air" nature of travelling in open-world games. Just get me to my location, ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. I only enjoyed [i]Dying Light[/i] and [i]Batman[/i]'s traversal because of the importance of XP, side conten…

claims.claim: Reviewers note that side missions and open-world activities in the game can feel repetitive.

citations.review_text:
If you're on the fence about picking this up, here is a breakdown of my experience after 45 hours and 100% completing both the main campaign and all the DLCs.

I ran this on an RTX 4070 Super at the absolute highest settings, and the port is flawless. I experienced zero bugs, crashes, stutters, or FPS drops. It is incredibly optimized and runs exactly how you'd want a modern PC port to run.

I highly recommend playing this with a controller. There is a slight learning curve at the very beginning, especially coming from a keyboard/mouse PC player, but once the controls click, it feels amazing. The web-swinging is incredibly fluid, and the combat is fast, smooth, and satisfying.

This is honestly one of the best-written versions of Peter Parker out there. The narrative is strong, and there is genuine, well-paced character development for both Peter and the rest of the supporting cast throughout the entire game.

I decided to grind out the side missions and extra tasks before moving heavily into the main story. They are definitely worth doing because they give you the resources needed to upgrade your gear. I will admit, doing the exact same tasks across every single district does get a little repetitive after a while, but the smooth gameplay loop makes the grind completely bearable.

Overall, an amazing superhero game that absolutely nails the feeling of being Spider-Man. Highly recommended.

Best Spider-man game to date(IMO).

An emotional and engaging story set in a beautiful recreation of New York City, packed with iconic landmarks and hidden lore to uncover through Spidey’s backpacks.

The open-world activities can feel a little repetitive, But the traversal alone is more than enough to make up for it. Swinging through the city is so much fun that even getting from point A to point B between activities never feels like a chore.

Verdict: Recommended with no issue. I had a great time with it and I am really looking forward to playing the next one. 

+ Positives +
+ Steam achievements (78, 2 playthroughs and all DLC)
+ All DLCs are included 
+ 47 suits to pick from 
+ 8 gadgets 
+ Tons of side activities and quests 
+ Amazing story (although it is kinda a Spider-Man cliché)
+ Great and fitting soundtrack 
+ Runs really well
+ You have ability to skip the puzzles if you wish
+ 8 years old and it still looks totally amazing 
+ Fun bosses
+ The city traversing is really fun 

– Negatives –
- No steam trading cards
- A lot of repetetive activities (especially for 100% crime)
- Higer difficuilty is just enemies hitting harder and having more hp 
- Graphic glitches (I had some fragmentation with max setting and ray tracing on)
- Crashed on me once
- Comic book clichés (some characters, like MJ, are basically having plot armor over their plot armor)

Fun Spider-Man gameplay, swinging around the city and fighting crime. Story was surprisingly well made for a licensed title and worth experiencing. Mission types apart from story and events around the city were very repetitive and near the 70% story mark I found myself wishing they would hurry up and end; can't recommend 100%-ing the map unless you really want it or have the patience of a monk. For a Route A playthrough of just story and maybe a handful of extra upgrades, can't recommend it enough.

Marvel's Spider-Man Remastered – The Definitive Way to Swing Through New York... Almost

When Marvel's Spider-Man first launched on PlayStation 4, it immediately established itself as one of the greatest superhero games ever made. The update to PS5 improved the graphics and framerate and now, the PC release of Marvel's Spider-Man Remastered takes that incredible foundation and elevates it with even higher frame rates, ultrawide support, customizable graphics settings, and some of the best web-swinging ever created. While a few technical quirks—particularly its HDR implementation—keep it from absolute perfection, this is still the best version of an outstanding game.

From the moment you leap off Avengers Tower and begin soaring through Manhattan, it's obvious why this game remains so beloved. The movement system is simply unmatched. Every swing builds momentum naturally, every dive feels exhilarating, and every rooftop launch makes traveling so enjoyable that fast travel almost feels unnecessary. Few games capture the fantasy of being a superhero as completely as Spider-Man Remastered.

Combat is equally exceptional. Similar to the free-flow style popularized by the Batman: Arkham series but refined with Spider-Man's speed and agility, every encounter becomes an exciting dance of dodges, aerial combos, gadgets, environmental takedowns, and perfectly timed finishers. As new abilities unlock, the combat continues to evolve without becoming overwhelming.

The story is another highlight. Rather than retelling Peter Parker's origin, Insomniac wisely presents an experienced Spider-Man balancing responsibility, relationships, and sacrifice. The writing treats its characters with respect, delivering emotional moments alongside blockbuster action.

Visually, the PC version is stunning. Manhattan comes alive with incredible detail, dense crowds, dynamic weather, and beautiful lighting. Running at high refresh rates transforms traversal into something that feels almost effortl…

citations.review_text: its just good, the taskmaster challenges are the hardest part. especially his boss fight

By the time I wrote this review, we all already know the reputation this game holds. It is one of, if not the best, Spider-Man experience available. The gameplay, the story, the mechanics, everything feels like specifically crafted to fit Spider-Man and it feels really refreshing to play even you have played dozens of open world games before. One thing that I think can be improved is to make it less hand-holding in certain situations. Just like any other open games, this game also litter the open world with collectibles and minigames but not to the point it becomes a cumbersome to collect, in fact you will feel like every collectibles and minigames feel rewarding, thanks to the best Spider-Man traversal system here. But, be warned, Taskmaster's challenge is the most frustrating thing to do in this game if you aim to 100% everything. If you persist, you will find the challenges are great actually in teaching you to be better in combat and web-swinging, even the stealth so don't just write it off early. Remember, don't just be great, be greater.

First ever game played on the PS4 and now I've completed the main story on my PC. Still got two more DLCs to finish after recently completing The Heist, also really well done (except the screwball challenges, i hate them)
